- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price spikes; forecasts often peak too early or too low relative to true price acceleration.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: tends to forecast prices back toward historical averages too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- When true prices rise sharply after a dip, model fails to anticipate the magnitude and duration of the spike, leading to underestimation.
- Model overcorrects after strong price increases, producing a “peak then drop” pattern that doesn’t match true price behavior.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 10 days, especially when recent history shows volatility or upward momentum.
- Model tends to underestimate the true price at the 15–20 day mark, often missing the “midpoint” of a trend that’s already established.
